chunks: Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from Zurārah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman to whom news of her husband's death was conveyed, so she observed her waiting period and married. Then her first husband came back, so he separated from her and the other also separated from her. How long should she observe a waiting period before becoming lawful for people?
He عليه السلام said: “Three menstrual cycles. Her womb is only cleared by three menstrual cycles, making her lawful for all people.”

key_terms.ثَلَاثَةَ قُرُوءٍ: three menstrual cycles as the prescribed ʿiddah here
key_terms.فَاعْتَدَّتْ: she observed the legally required waiting period
key_terms.نُعِيَ: news was conveyed of someone's death
key_terms.يُسْتَبْرَأُ: is cleared or verified to be free, referring to the womb

ai.seo_question: How long is the ʿiddah for a woman who remarried after false news of her husband's death and then separated from both husbands?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling regarding a woman who remarried after being informed of her husband's death, only for the first husband to return. The Imam عليه السلام rules that after separation she must observe an ʿiddah of three qurūʾ, because that period establishes clearance of the womb and makes remarriage permissible.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4888 - Musa ibn Bakr narrated from Zurara who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a woman who was informed that her husband had passed away, so she observed her waiting period (iddah) and remarried. Then her first husband returned, leading both her first and second husbands to separate from her. I asked how long she should observe the waiting period for people (before remarrying).
Imam (as) said: "Three menstrual cycles (qur). Indeed, her womb is cleared after three menstrual cycles, which makes her lawful for all men."
